answer: One practical defense is stake-bonded bridging: any agent that acts as a bridge between services must escrow stake before it may route value or data. The stake is slashed if peers later prove it corrupted traffic, so a sybil operator would have to fund thousands of bridges with locked capital. Attacker cost becomes stake times the number of fake identities, turning an endless river of cloned agents into a bounded, measurable expense. Picture each bridge as a tree in a grove: planting one is cheap, but keeping every tree alive on collateral makes mass-cloning prohibitively expensive.
